criteria_results.title: §2(a): Restore 'entitlement order' language
criteria_results.reasoning: The redline expressly restores “Entitlement Order” language in Section 2.2, defines the term by reference to UCC § 8-102(a)(8), and requires the Bank to comply with Secured Party entitlement orders under the Article 8 framework. It therefore rejects an instruction-only formulation.

criteria_results.title: Cover note explains §2(a) entitlement order position
criteria_results.reasoning: The cover note expressly addresses the Section 2 entitlement-order versus instruction change, states that Pinnacle restored the entitlement-order language while retaining Article 9 instruction language (thereby rejecting the Bank’s substitution), and explains the UCC Article 8 control and perfection rationale for the dual-track formulation.

criteria_results.title: §2(b): Address springing exclusive control and reject broad Bank carve-out
criteria_results.reasoning: The redline preserves springing exclusive control triggered by receipt of an NOEC while expressly limiting Graycliff’s operating rights to the pre-NOEC period. It rejects the broad post-NOEC carve-out by extinguishing Graycliff’s instruction rights and requiring the Bank to cease accepting new Graycliff instructions and comply exclusively with the Secured Party, subject only to a narrow transition for previously initiated items.

criteria_results.title: §3: Reject Bank set-off priority over Secured Party instructions
criteria_results.reasoning: The redline expressly deletes the Bank language making its set-off rights prior to Secured Party instructions and replaces it with a conflicting-instructions waterfall under which Secured Party instructions control at all times, subject only to narrowly limited set-off exceptions. It also generally subordinates Bank liens and waives broad set-off rights.

criteria_results.title: §4: Narrow expanded self-help set-off to direct, liquidated obligations
criteria_results.reasoning: The redline deletes the Bank’s broad set-off right covering “any obligation” whether direct or contingent and replaces it with a narrow right limited to direct, matured, liquidated obligations arising under the deposit account agreements, specifically customary account maintenance/service fees and returned or charged-back items. It also expressly excludes contingent, unmatured, lending, treasury-management, derivatives, foreign-exchange, and affiliate obligations.

criteria_results.title: §5: Propose 3-business-day NOEC compliance period
criteria_results.reasoning: The redline expressly deletes the Bank’s five-Business-Day period and replaces it with a three-Business-Day NOEC compliance period, rather than restoring the original two-Business-Day period.

criteria_results.title: §6: Reject indemnification coverage for Bank gross negligence
criteria_results.reasoning: The redline expressly rejects indemnification for Bank gross negligence and restores an exclusion for losses resulting from the Bank indemnitee’s gross negligence, willful misconduct, or fraud. This satisfies the criterion.

criteria_results.title: §7(a): Reject $50,000 aggregate liability cap
criteria_results.reasoning: The redline expressly rejects and deletes the $50,000 aggregate liability cap in full, stating that no aggregate dollar cap applies to the Bank’s liability.

criteria_results.title: §7(b): Address mutual consequential/punitive/indirect damages waiver
criteria_results.reasoning: The output expressly addresses the mutual consequential, punitive, and indirect damages waiver in Item 8, retaining it unchanged for discussion while reserving Pinnacle’s right to revisit it. The cover note also explains this position.

criteria_results.title: Cover note confirms position on §7(b) mutual damages waiver
criteria_results.reasoning: The cover note expressly addresses the mutual consequential, punitive, and indirect damages waiver in item 8. It states that the waiver is retained for discussion for this turn, while qualifying that Pinnacle reserves the right to revisit it and that retention is not final acceptance of the overall limitations package.

criteria_results.title: §8: Reject 90-day lookback; propose full subordination or 180-day lookback
criteria_results.reasoning: The redline expressly rejects the Bank’s 90-day lookback and replaces it with a 180-day lookback in the Bank-lien subordination provision, satisfying the criterion’s minimum requirement.

criteria_results.title: §9: Reject 30-day unilateral termination; propose 90-day notice with transition rights
criteria_results.reasoning: The redline expressly deletes the Bank’s unilateral 30-day termination right and replaces it with at least 90 days’ prior written notice. It also grants the Secured Party express transition rights, requires the Bank’s reasonable cooperation, and keeps the Bank bound until replacement accounts and a replacement control agreement are in place unless the Secured Party agrees otherwise.

criteria_results.title: §10: Restore New York governing law
criteria_results.reasoning: The redline expressly deletes North Carolina governing law and restores New York governing law in the governing-law provision. The cover note likewise states that Pinnacle rejects the Bank’s North Carolina change and restores New York law.

criteria_results.title: Cover note acknowledges New York governing law is strongly preferred with possible flexibility
criteria_results.reasoning: The cover note expressly states that Pinnacle restored and prefers New York governing law and venue, explaining that alignment with the Credit Agreement reduces uncertainty. Although it does not expressly offer flexibility if this is a deal-breaker, the criterion is satisfied by clearly indicating New York is preferred.

criteria_results.title: §12: Restore no-prior-control-agreement representation
criteria_results.reasoning: The redline restores the Bank’s representation that no other person has control, that the Bank has not entered into another control agreement, and that it has received no notice of any other lien or adverse claim affecting the accounts.

criteria_results.title: §13: Restore successor-bank notification obligation
criteria_results.reasoning: The redline restores Section 9’s successor-bank notification obligation. It requires the Bank to give the Secured Party at least 30 days’ prior written notice before transferring the Accounts or its obligations, merging, consolidating, or transferring deposit-taking operations or assets to a successor institution, and also requires successor assumption mechanics.

criteria_results.title: §11: Accept annual maintenance fee but negotiate down $15,000 legal-fee reimbursement
criteria_results.reasoning: The redline expressly accepts the $3,500 annual maintenance fee per account ($10,500 total for three accounts) and negotiates the one-time legal-fee reimbursement down from $15,000 to the lesser of $7,500 or reasonable, documented, out-of-pocket outside legal costs.

criteria_results.title: ACA maintains form and substance satisfactory to Administrative Agent
criteria_results.reasoning: The counter-turn preserves the core UCC control mechanics: it restores both Article 9 “Instruction” and applicable Article 8 “Entitlement Order” terminology, requires compliance without further debtor consent, terminates the Depositor’s operational authority following an NOEC, gives Secured Party instructions priority, and limits Bank set-off to narrow deposit-account obligations. The three-Business-Day implementation provision does not negate the Bank’s unconditional agreement to comply or otherwise undermine perfection.

criteria_results.title: Cover note maintains professional and cordial tone
criteria_results.reasoning: The cover note is formal, respectful, and appropriately cordial for inter-counsel negotiations. It thanks opposing counsel, explains each position in measured language, acknowledges the Bank’s legitimate concerns, proposes compromises, and invites further discussion, while remaining clear and firm on Pinnacle’s non-negotiable control, liability, and indemnification positions.
